items.stem: Draw a schematic diagram of a circuit consisting of a battery of six 2 V cells, a 6 Ω resistor, a 12 Ω resistor and an 18 Ω resistor and a plug key, all connected in series. Calculate the following (when the key is closed): (i) Electric current flowing in the circuit. (ii) Potential difference across the 18 Ω resistor. (iii) Electric power consumed in the 18 Ω resistor.
items.answer: The circuit is drawn as one series loop containing the six 2 V cells (total 12 V), the plug key and the three resistors. Since all the resistances are in series, R_eq = 6 + 12 + 18 = 36 Ω. (i) I = V/R_eq = 12/36 = 1/3 A ≈ 0.33 A. (ii) V₁₈ = IR = (1/3) × 18 = 6 V. (iii) P₁₈ = I²R = (1/3)² × 18 = 2 W.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode (Ω, subscripts). The figure printed beside the solution is the diagram the question asks the student to draw, so no image is attached.

items.stem: (i) What is meant by resistance of a conductor? Define its SI unit. (ii) List two factors on which the resistance of a rectangular conductor depends. (iii) How will the resistance of a wire be affected if (1) its length is doubled, and (2) its radius is also doubled? Give justification for your answer.
items.answer: (i) Resistance is the property of a conductor by which it resists the flow of charge through it. Numerically it is the ratio of the potential difference across the conductor to the current flowing through it. Its SI unit is the ohm (Ω): a conductor has a resistance of 1 ohm if a current of 1 ampere flows through it when the potential difference across it is 1 volt. (ii) The resistance depends on (1) the length of the conductor and (2) the area of cross-section of the conductor. (iii) (1) Resistance is directly proportional to length, so if the length is doubled the resistance is also doubled. (2) Resistance is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section; if the radius is doubled the area becomes four times larger, so the resistance becomes one-fourth.
items.ocr: Printed stem breaks as 'if its.' before listing the two changes; read as 'if (1) its length is doubled, and (2) its radius is also doubled'. The answer tag prints damaged as 'Ans : (a (i)'.

items.stem: (a) Write the mathematical expression for Joule's law of heating. (b) Compute the heat generated while transferring 96000 coulomb of charge in two hours through a potential difference of 40 V.
items.answer: (a) According to Joule's law of heating, the heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to (i) the square of the current I for a given resistance, (ii) the resistance R for a given current, and (iii) the time t for which the current flows. Mathematically, H = I²Rt. (b) Given q = 96000 C, t = 2 h = 120 min = 7200 s and V = 40 V. Heat H = VIt, and I = q/t, so H = V × (q/t) × t = Vq = 40 × 96000 = 3840000 J = 3840 kJ.

items.stem: Two electric lamps rated 100 W, 220 V and 25 W, 220 V are connected in parallel. Calculate the total electric current in the circuit.
items.answer: For the first bulb, R₁ = V²/P₁ = (220)²/100 = 484 Ω. For the second bulb, R₂ = V²/P₂ = (220)²/25 = 1936 Ω. When connected in parallel, 1/R = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ = 1/484 + 1/1936 = 5/1936, so R = 1936/5 = 387.2 Ω. Total current I = V/R = 220/387.2 = 0.56 A.

items.stem: Calculate the total cost of running the following electrical devices in the month of September, if the rate of 1 unit of electricity is ₹6.00. (i) Electric heater of 1000 W for 5 hours daily. (ii) Electric refrigerator of 400 W for 10 hours daily.
items.answer: (i) Energy consumed by the electric heater per day = P × t = 1000 × 5 = 5000 Wh. (ii) Energy consumed by the refrigerator per day = P × t = 400 × 10 = 4000 Wh. Total energy consumed in one day = 5000 + 4000 = 9000 Wh = 9 kWh. September has 30 days, so the energy consumed in the month = 9 × 30 = 270 kWh = 270 units. Cost of 1 unit = ₹6, so the total cost = 6 × 270 = ₹1,620.

items.stem: (a) In a given ammeter, a student saw that the needle indicates the 12th division while performing an experiment to verify Ohm's law. If the ammeter has 10 divisions between 0 and 0.5 A, then what is the ammeter reading corresponding to the 12th division? (b) How do you connect an ammeter and a voltmeter in an electric circuit?
items.answer: (a) Least count of the ammeter = 0.5 A ÷ 10 divisions = 0.05 A per division. Reading at the 12th division = 12 × 0.05 = 0.6 A. (b) An ammeter is always connected in series with the element whose current is to be measured, and a voltmeter is always connected in parallel across the element whose potential difference is to be measured.
items.ocr: The printed solution for this question is absent from the extraction - page 38 opens directly with the answer of Q254 - so the answer here is worked from the printed data (least count 0.05 A, 12 divisions = 0.6 A) and the standard ammeter/voltmeter connection rule.

items.stem: Draw a circuit diagram of an electric circuit containing a cell, a key, an ammeter, a resistor of 4 Ω in series with a combination of two resistors (8 Ω each) in parallel and a voltmeter across the parallel combination. Each of them dissipates maximum energy and can withstand a maximum power of 16 W without melting. Find the maximum current that can flow through the three resistors.
items.answer: We know P = I²R, so I = √(P/R). With P = 16 W, the maximum current through the 4 Ω resistor is I = √(16/4) = 2 A. This 2 A divides equally between the two identical 8 Ω resistors in parallel, so the current through each 8 Ω resistor is ½ × 2 = 1 A.

items.stem: State the factors on which the resistance of a cylindrical conductor depends. How will the resistance of a conductor change if it is stretched so that its length is doubled?
items.answer: The resistance of a cylindrical conductor is directly proportional to its length l and inversely proportional to its area of cross-section A, i.e. R ∝ l and R ∝ 1/A. Combining, R ∝ l/A, so R = ρl/A, where ρ is the resistivity of the material. On stretching, the volume of the wire stays constant, so Al = A′(2l), giving A′ = A/2. The new resistance R′ = ρ(2l)/(A/2) = 4ρl/A = 4R, i.e. 4 times the original resistance.
items.ocr: LaTeX rewritten to Unicode; the printed line 'Al = Al′' is the volume-conservation step written correctly in the next line as Al = A′(2l).

items.answer: Plotting V (y-axis) against I (x-axis) gives a straight line passing through the origin, which shows that V ∝ I. Taking a pair of values from the graph, R = V/I = 3.3/1.0 = 3.3 Ω. So the resistance of the resistor is about 3.3 Ω (ohm).

items.stem: A metallic coil, connected to a 220 V supply, has a resistance of 110 ohm (while hot). How long will it take for this coil to heat 1 kg of water from 20 °C to 70 °C? Assume that the whole of the heat produced by the coil is taken up by the water. (Specific heat of water = 4186 J/kg °C)
items.answer: Power of the coil, P = V²/R = (220)²/110 = 440 W, so the heat supplied in time t is Energy = P × t = 440t joules. Heat required by the water: m = 1 kg, Δt = (70 − 20) °C = 50 °C, so Q = msΔt = 1 × 4186 × 50 = 209300 J. Equating the two, 440t = 209300, hence t = 209300/440 = 475.6 s (about 7 minutes 56 seconds).

items.stem: State Joule's law of heating. List two special characteristics of a heating element wire. An electric iron consumes energy at the rate of 880 W when the heating is at the maximum rate and 440 W when the heating is at the minimum rate. The applied voltage is 220 V. Calculate the current and resistance in each case.
items.answer: Joule's law: if a current I flows through a resistor of resistance R for a time t, the heat produced in the resistor is H = I²Rt joules. Two characteristics of a heating element wire: (i) it must not melt at high temperature (high melting point), and (ii) it has high resistivity. For the electric iron, V = 220 V. At the maximum rate: I = P/V = 880/220 = 4 A and R = V/I = 220/4 = 55 Ω. At the minimum rate: I = 440/220 = 2 A and R = 220/2 = 110 Ω.
items.ocr: The printed solution works with 'Net Power = P_max − P_min = VI' and so produces only one pair of values (I = 2 A, R = 110 Ω). Since the question asks for each case, both cases are worked here from P = VI; the minimum-rate values agree with the printed ones.

items.stem: Study the given electric circuit and calculate (i) the current flowing through the 4 Ω resistor and (ii) the potential difference across the combination of the two resistors of 8 Ω each.
items.answer: (i) From V = IR, 2 V = I × 4 Ω, so I = 0.5 A. (ii) The two 8 Ω resistors are in parallel, so 1/R_eq = 1/8 + 1/8 = 2/8 = 1/4, giving R_eq = 4 Ω. This parallel combination is in series with the 4 Ω resistor, so R_total = 4 + 4 = 8 Ω and the total current I_total = V/R = 2/8 = 1/4 A. The potential difference across the parallel combination = I_total × R_eq = (1/4) × 4 = 1 V.
items.ocr: Printed part (i) puts the whole 2 V across the 4 Ω resistor (0.5 A) while part (ii) uses the series total current (0.25 A); both are kept as printed. The last printed line writes the product as a fraction (I_total/R_eq) but evaluates it as I_total × R_eq = 1 V. 'resister' corrected to 'resistor'.

items.stem: What would be the reading of the ammeter and the voltmeter in the given circuit?
items.answer: Here R₁ = 1 Ω and R₂ = 2 Ω are connected in series, so the equivalent resistance R = R₁ + R₂ = 1 + 2 = 3 Ω. Current I = V/R = 3/3 = 1 A, so the ammeter reading = 1 A. The voltmeter is connected across the 2 Ω resistor, so the voltmeter reading = IR = 1 × 2 = 2 V.

items.stem: (a) Define the SI unit of potential difference. (b) Calculate the potential difference between the terminals of a battery if 100 joules of work is required to transfer 20 coulombs of charge from one terminal of the battery to the other.
items.answer: (a) The volt is the SI unit of potential difference. The potential difference between two points is said to be 1 volt if 1 joule of work is done in carrying 1 coulomb of positive charge from one point to the other. (b) The relation between work W, charge Q and potential difference V is V = W/Q. Given W = 100 J and Q = 20 C, V = 100/20 = 5 V.

items.stem: For the circuit diagram given below, calculate (a) the value of current through each resistor, (b) the total current in the circuit, and (c) the total effective resistance of the circuit.
items.answer: (a) The three resistances shown are joined in parallel, so the voltage across each of them is the same, 6 V. I₁ = V/R₁ = 6/5 = 1.2 A through R₁ = 5 Ω; I₂ = V/R₂ = 6/10 = 0.6 A through R₂ = 10 Ω; I₃ = V/R₃ = 6/30 = 0.2 A through R₃ = 30 Ω. (b) Total current I = I₁ + I₂ + I₃ = 1.2 + 0.6 + 0.2 = 2.0 A. (c) Total effective resistance R_eq = V/I = 6/2.0 = 3.0 Ω.

items.stem: (a) Two conductors A and B of resistances 5 Ω and 10 Ω respectively can be arranged in parallel and later on in series. In each arrangement, the total voltage applied across it is 20 volts. In which arrangement will the voltage across A and B be the same and in which case will the current flowing through A and B be the same? (b) Calculate the total resistance for each arrangement.
items.answer: (a) The voltage across A and B will be the same in the parallel arrangement; the current flowing through A and B will be the same in the series arrangement. (b) Equivalent resistance in series = (5 + 10) Ω = 15 Ω. Equivalent resistance in parallel: 1/R = 1/5 + 1/10 = 3/10, so R = 10/3 = 3.33 Ω.

items.stem: V–I graph for a conductor is as shown in the figure. (i) What do you infer from this graph? (ii) State the law expressed here. (iii) Name the physical quantity represented by the slope of this graph and its unit.
items.answer: (i) The graph is a straight line passing through the origin, so the inference is V ∝ I. (ii) The law states that the current passing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends, provided the physical conditions such as temperature and density remain unchanged. This is Ohm's law. (iii) The slope of the graph represents the resistance of the conductor, and the unit of resistance is the ohm (Ω).
items.ocr: The three parts of the stem print at the top of page 38, far from the numbered line '254. V-I graph for a conductor is as shown in figure' and its figure on page 41; rejoined. The printed inference 'V ? I' is 'V ∝ I'; 'unchanges' read as 'unchanged'.

items.stem: State the formula co-relating the electric current flowing in a conductor and the voltage applied across it. Also show this relationship by drawing a graph. What would be the resistance of a conductor if the current flowing through it is 0.35 ampere when the potential difference across it is 1.4 volt?
items.answer: Ohm's law states that, physical conditions remaining the same, the current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference applied across its two ends: V ∝ I, i.e. V = IR. The graph of V against I is a straight line passing through the origin. Given V = 1.4 volt and I = 0.35 A, the resistance R = V/I = 1.4/0.35 = 4 Ω.
items.ocr: The graph printed with the answer belongs to the worked solution, so no image is attached.

items.stem: Derive an expression for the equivalent resistance when two resistors of resistance R₁ and R₂ are connected in parallel.
items.answer: Consider two resistances R₁ and R₂ connected in parallel across a potential difference V. When the current I reaches the junction a, it splits into I₁ through R₁ and I₂ through R₂. Since charge is conserved, the current entering a equals the current leaving it: I = I₁ + I₂ ...(1). As the resistors are in parallel, the potential difference across each is the same, so by Ohm's law I₁ = V/R₁ and I₂ = V/R₂. Substituting in (1), I = V/R₁ + V/R₂ ...(2). If R_p is the equivalent resistance of the combination, then I = V/R_p ...(3). From (2) and (3), V/R_p = V/R₁ + V/R₂, hence 1/R_p = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂.

items.stem: A wire of resistance 6 Ω is bent to form a closed square. What is the resistance across a diagonal of the square?
items.answer: Total resistance of the wire = 6 Ω. The four sides of the square are equal, AB = BC = CD = AD, so each side has resistance R₁ = R₂ = R₃ = R₄ = 6/4 = 1.5 Ω. Across the diagonal AC the square splits into two arms in parallel: R′ = 1.5 + 1.5 = 3 Ω and R″ = 1.5 + 1.5 = 3 Ω. Then 1/R = 1/3 + 1/3 = 2/3, so R = 3/2 = 1.5 Ω.

items.stem: A hot plate of an electric oven, connected to a 200 V line, has two resistance coils A and B each of 30 Ω, which may be used separately, in series or in parallel. Find the value of the current required in each of the three cases.
items.answer: Taking V = 220 V as used throughout the worked solution, with R_A = R_B = 30 Ω: (i) When coil A or B is used separately, I = V/R = 220/30 = 7.33 A. (ii) When the coils are in series, R_s = R_A + R_B = 30 + 30 = 60 Ω, so I_s = 220/60 = 3.67 A. (iii) When the coils are in parallel, 1/R_p = 1/30 + 1/30 = 1/15, so R_p = 15 Ω and I_p = 220/15 = 14.67 A.
items.ocr: The stem says the hot plate is connected to a 200 V line but the worked solution opens 'Given V = 220 Volt' and uses 220 V in all three cases; the solution wins, so the currents quoted are for 220 V (at 200 V they would be 6.67 A, 3.33 A and 13.33 A).
